DD_DE.9Feb: About four-to-six destroyer-equivalent close-fire assignments can transition to replenishment, escort or ASW after secure confirmation.
DD_DE.10_11Feb: A further two-to-four equivalent direct-fire assignments can be released as unloading and pocket risk decline.
DD_DE.retained: Outer ASW/picket/transport-screen demand remains high; support release is not a wholesale withdrawal of escort.

CVE.9_10Feb: Roughly two-to-three CVE-equivalent daily sortie wallets shift from CAS/spotting toward CAP, ASW, ferry and replenishment.
CVE.10_12Feb: Roughly four-to-five CVE-equivalent wallets can enter follow-on/replenishment planning, while one-to-two equivalent wallets remain local for cover, search, ferry and residual support.
CVE.guard: Aircraft and deck availability remain limited by ammunition, fuel, maintenance and aircrew cycle; task release is not instant full-deck readiness.

old_BB_CA_fire_support.state: Major direct-fire demand collapses after 9-Feb secure, but many ships require ammunition replenishment, barrel/gear checks, fuel and re-formation.
old_BB_CA_fire_support.follow_on_ready_gate: Selected heavy fire-support elements can be ready for a new assault support concentration around 12-15 Feb, not on the morning secure is declared.

amphibious_shipping.state: Unloading, casualty evacuation, vehicle recovery, repair and reloading continue through roughly 10-13 Feb. The 5-Feb mission-killed LST reduces margin but does not halt follow-on planning.
amphibious_shipping.effect: Catchpole-type assault cannot be inferred solely from ground secure date; landing-shipping turnaround remains a schedule gate.
